Project

2026-10-02

project.Rmd

Project

Projects in Synapse are “containers” that group relevant content and people together. All data must be uploaded into a project. Projects can be private so only you can see the contents, they can be shared with your collaborators, or they can be made public so anyone on the web can view your research.

Tutorial purpose

In this vignette you will:

  1. Create a new project
  2. Print stored attributes about your project
  3. Get an existing project

Prerequisites

  1. Make sure that you have completed the Installation setup.
  2. Make sure that you have completed the Authentication setup.

1. Create a new project 

library(synapser)
## 
## TERMS OF USE NOTICE:
##   When using Synapse, remember that the terms and conditions of use require that you:
##   1) Attribute data contributors when discussing these data or results from these data.
##   2) Not discriminate, identify, or recontact individuals or groups represented by the data.
##   3) Use and contribute only data de-identified to HIPAA standards.
##   4) Redistribute data only under these same terms of use.
synLogin()
## Welcome, Dan Lu!
## NULL

# Project names must be globally unique
project_name = paste0(
  "My uniquely named project about Alzheimer's Disease ",
  paste(sample(c(letters, LETTERS, 0:9), 8, replace = TRUE), collapse = "")
)
project = Project(name = project_name) |> synStore()
cat("Created project:", project$id, "\n")
## Created project: syn77515198

Now that you have created your project you are able to inspect the project in the Synapse web UI.

2. Print stored attributes about your project 

cat("My project ID is:", project$id, "\n")
## My project ID is: syn77515198
cat("I created my project on:", project$created_on, "\n")
## I created my project on: 2026-09-21T04:24:40.732Z
cat("The ID of the user that created my project is:", project$created_by, "\n")
## The ID of the user that created my project is: 3434599
cat("My project was last modified on:", project$modified_on, "\n")
## My project was last modified on: 2026-09-21T04:24:40.732Z
You’ll notice the output looks like: 
My project ID is: syn12345678
I created my project on: 2000-01-01T12:00:00.001Z
The ID of the user that created my project is: 1234567
My project was last modified on: 2000-01-01T12:00:00.001Z

Find all of the available attributes about your project in the Project reference documentation.

3. Get an existing project

Each Project only needs to be created once. Since you’ve already created it you can access it again by retrieving it using its name.

my_project_object = Project(name = project_name) |> synGet()
cat("I just got my project:", my_project_object$name, ", id:", my_project_object$id, "\n")
## I just got my project: My uniquely named project about Alzheimer's Disease SwlKLUUE , id: syn77515198
The result will look like: 
I just got my project: My uniquely named project about Alzheimer's Disease, id: syn12345678

Clean Up

Delete the project and all its contents when done:

synDelete(project)
